clue.text: Playwright's issue is catching

definitions.note: the playwright of this puzzle is Shakespeare; his sonnets are among his works

parts.note: issue means offspring, here a son
nets means catches, as a fisherman does

explanation.surface: A dramatist's child has come down with something infectious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playwright's' throughout this puzzle stands for Shakespeare's, so the definition asks for one of his works.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Sonnets, the 154 poems of 1609, are a famous body of the playwright's writing.

clue.text: Late love leaves right away

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right goes missing from the foliage word

parts.note: verdure is green foliage, a mass of leaves

explanation.surface: A tardy lover walks out on the right moment immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by the expected time, so it is late.

clue.text: Actor working 9-5?

indicators.note: working here means set in motion and rearranged, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the number nine spelt out as a word
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Is this performer someone with an ordinary office-hours job?
explanation.walkthrough: '9-5' reads as office hours, but it gives NINE and V, which 'working' rearranges. David Niven was a British film star.
explanation.definitionFit: David Niven was a celebrated British film actor of the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Author of Months and nothing else — ie Seasons

indicators.note: else means otherwise, so the letters are put together otherwise than printed

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A writer who produced nothing but calendar months, as in a book of seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ie Seasons' is a pointer to the work: James Thomson wrote The Seasons (1730), a poem cycle through the year.
explanation.definitionFit: James Thomson, Scottish poet, wrote The Seasons and the words of Rule, Britannia.

clue.text: Try one who won't drink to entertain the locum

parts.note: one as the indefinite article, a

indicators.note: entertain means take in as a guest, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
a locum is a stand-in doctor, a temp

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is put on trial for hosting the stand-in doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like a court case but means an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To attempt something is to try it; both are verbs of making an effort.

clue.text: Playwright's partner of 20 has a turn

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's poem pairs a mythical bird of fire with this creature in The Phoenix and the ...
a boat that capsizes is said to turn this way, upside down like a sea reptile on its back

explanation.walkthrough: 20 is PHOENIX: Shakespeare's poem The Phoenix and the Turtle (the turtle-dove). 'Turn turtle' means to capsize.
explanation.definitionFit: The turtle-dove is the Phoenix's partner in Shakespeare's poem, and turning turtle is overturning.

clue.text: Piece work included in flight

indicators.note: included in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an element is a component piece of something
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Piecework was part of the escape plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is running away, here to marry in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is a flight from home to marry without consent.

clue.text: See 9
Collection attributed to playwright by press legitimation? Pah!

annotationWithheld.why: Collection attributed to playwright by press legitimation? Pah! (3,10,7): anagram of PRESS LEGITIMATION PAH with no anagram indicator word; only the doubt in '? Pah!' implies it, and 'Pah' is also fodder
annotationWithheld.clue: Collection attributed to playwright by press legitimation? Pah!

clue.text: Fuel provider variously contains it

indicators.note: contains it says the answer sits inside the words that follow on the page

explanation.surface: A fuel supplier stocks it in various forms.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is British diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is a British name for diesel oil used as road-vehicle fuel.

clue.text: Row with the Lord about heaven?

indicators.note: about means around and in disorder, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone is arguing with God about paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the two parts of the fodder, ROW and THE LORD, which 'about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The other world is the afterlife or spiritual realm, and heaven is an example of it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Playwright's partner of 25 has trouble with wrong return

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in Much Ado About Nothing

indicators.note: return says this word is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's companion character is in trouble for doing wrong again.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is VENUS: Shakespeare's poem Venus and Adonis.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis is paired with the goddess in Shakespeare's narrative poem Venus and Adonis.

clue.text: Cornish game in which some people make mistakes

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a Cornish place, the noun answer

indicators.note: in which says the game holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: some takes just a part of the next word, its first letter

parts.note: to err is to make mistakes

explanation.surface: A game in Cornwall where some players keep slipping up.
explanation.walkthrough: POLPERRO is a fishing village in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Polperro is a picturesque fishing village on the south coast of Cornwall.

clue.text: Admit legality of maverick Coe's reign

indicators.note: a maverick is unorthodox and wayward, so the letters run wild

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the athlete and sports administrator, with the possessive 's kept as a letter

explanation.surface: The legitimacy of Lord Coe's unorthodox reign is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maverick' rearranges COES and REIGN together.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise a state or government is to admit formally that it is legitimate.

clue.text: See 18
Good girl of 26's is a girl that's budding

parts.note: 26 is Jane Austen, whose heroine Emma names one of her novels

explanation.surface: A nice young woman from an Austen novel is a girl coming into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: A gemma is a bud or budlike growth in botany, and also a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is both a girl's name and the botanical term for a bud that grows into a new plant.

clue.text: No moving spirit from here

definitions.meaning: the apparatus that distils spirits such as whisky

explanation.definitionFit: Still means motionless, and a still is the distilling apparatus that spirit comes from.

clue.text: Playwright's treatment cut short by enemy returning money to church

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: therapy is medical treatment

indicators.note: returning says the word for enemy is read backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
lucre is money, especially ill-gotten
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A dramatist's course of therapy is curtailed by a foe giving cash back to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playwright's' means a work by Shakespeare: his narrative poem of 1594.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rape of Lucrece is a long narrative poem published by Shakespeare in 1594.

clue.text: Putin speaking French? I'm not accepting that!

annotationWithheld.why: Putin speaking French? I'm not accepting that! (9): PUT inside DISANT (French 'speaking'), but 'Putin' gives both PUT and the container signal 'in', one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Putin speaking French? I'm not accepting that!

clue.text: False hope — nothing's coming from Arizona

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters of the next word are faked into a new order

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: No hope at all coming from the desert state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' rearranges HOPE to PHOE. Phoenix is the capital of Arizona; it is also 6's partner in Shakespeare's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix is the state capital of Arizona, so it is a city that comes from that state.

clue.text: Tell of animal in Arne's work

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
work as in workings over, so the composer's name is rearranged

parts.note: Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Describe the creature in a piece by Arne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges ARNE to NARE, which holds RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or give an account.

clue.text: Quiet! Quiet! Play the game!

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly, in music

indicators.note: play means move about loosely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shushes the room twice and says to get on with the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Piquet is a card game for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is a seventeenth-century card game for two people, played with a short pack.

clue.text: Trojan exchanged in a truce

indicators.note: exchanged means swapped around, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A Trojan prisoner is swapped during a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: Teucer was the first king of Troy, so Teucrian is a poetic word for Trojan.
explanation.definitionFit: Teucrian means Trojan, from Teucer, a legendary early king of Troy.

clue.text: Turn to face the plain holding baby's head

indicators.note: holding says the first word contains the other letter

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Turn round on the flat land while holding the infant's head.
explanation.walkthrough: To obvert is to turn something so that its front faces you.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvert means to turn so as to present a different face or surface.

clue.text: (I) have gone round the sun

parts.note: I've shortened, the contracted ending 've

indicators.note: gone round means turned about, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having travelled round the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the planet speaking, the whole clue describes its orbit; 25 is also Adonis's partner in Shakespeare's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the second planet from the sun, which it orbits like the other planets.

clue.text: Writer of the month has had us in for a meal

parts.note: Jan is the abbreviation for January

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to have had a meal is to have eaten
taken as written

explanation.surface: This month's featured author invited us round for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a meal' tells us 'had' means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen was the English novelist of Pride and Prejudice and Emma.

clue.text: Wasn't he satisfied with the flood warning?

definitions.text: Wasn't he satisfied with the flood warning?

parts.words: Wasn't he satisfied with the flood warning?
parts.note: the biblical patriarch warned of the deluge and built an ark; a satisfied person might say 'no' and 'ah'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface has someone heeding a flood alert; the biblical ark-builder was the one forewarned of the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch of Genesis was warned by God of the Flood and built the ark.

clue.text: … x 2.5 — that's what happens in heartless heaven

definitions.note: the ellipsis continues from the clue's own number, 28

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: the sky is the heavens
an event is something that happens

explanation.surface: Something is multiplied, and it occurs in a hollowed-out sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis stands for the clue number: 28 times 2.5 is 70.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-eight multiplied by two and a half gives the number seventy.

clue.text: Was the journalist discriminating against women going topless?

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: sexist means prejudiced on grounds of sex
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist

explanation.surface: Was the newspaper man sexist for having women go topless?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' is the definition, though it reads as the start of a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Existed and was are both past forms meaning had being or was present.
